question.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{(-4)\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-6\,}{\,\,2\,}b \\  & =-3b \\  & =-3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
